title: I Used the Cruise Muster-Station Photo After They Moved My Cabin Twice

parts.text: I mustered at station G at 4:10 p.m. with the life vest from cabin 8122. Guest services had already moved me to 8140, then 6201, because a family wanted connecting rooms. I was forty-one, traveling alone with a wheelchair-accessible booking I had paid for. The new cabin had a lip at the bathroom I could not roll over. I photographed the muster card, both keys, and the lip. The agent smiled. "It's the same ship." I asked her to stand in the photo. She declined. Then the captain's drill called 6201 to station C, which was two decks and a jammed elevator away. My original station G was still printed on the first key card they forgot to kill.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Drill is live; the working key still sends me to G and the cabin I cannot use.

social.video_title: They moved my accessible cabin and left the old muster key alive — Part 1/2
social.description: Two moves, a bathroom lip, station C versus G. The first key still worked. Would you have gone to the drill?

parts.text: I rolled to guest services with both keys during the drill, which is the only time managers appear. They restored 8122. The family kept 8140 without connecting. I sent the lip photo to the accessibility desk on shore. A credit posted before formal night. Station G knew my name again. The killed key is in my toiletry bag as a souvenir of how the same ship is not the same bathroom. I mustered on time. That was never the problem.

social.video_title: 8122 came back before formal night — Part 2/2
social.description: Restored cabin, shore credit, a dead key in the toiletry bag. Was connecting rooms a wheelchair?
